title: Pochettino assistants leave USMNT camp early to go to Manchester United: Sources
content:
U.S. national team assistant coaches Jesús Pérez, Toni Jiménez and Sebastiano Pochettino departed the U.S. camp on Saturday night to fly to Manchester, where they’ll begin work at Manchester United, sources briefed on the situation tell The Athletic.

The USMNT beat Haiti 6-0 in leg one of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals on Saturday. With such a cushion entering Tuesday night’s second leg, U.S. Soccer agreed to let Mauricio Pochettino’s assistants leave early. If the scoreline was closer, they wouldn’t have left, sources say, although Pochettino indicated in his pre-match press conference on Monday that it was pre-planned regardless of Saturday night’s result.

It was announced last week that Pochettino will be leaving the U.S. to take the coaching job at Manchester United three months after he signed a new four-year deal with U.S. Soccer following the World Cup, and his staff will be accompanying him at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will remain on the sideline for the USMNT for his final match in charge against Haiti in Cincinnati, where he attended the Sunday Night Football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals last night. He will depart for Manchester after the match to join his assistants and begin preparations for his first game in charge for United against Liverpool on Sunday.

“[The assistants] are ahead. After the game they flew to to Manchester and they are there in advance,” Pochettino said. “That was the plan when we agreed terms with with Manchester United and with the national team. They are (there) in advance. They are preparing because Wednesday when (we) will arrive … it’s going to be nonstop, and then start with playing games.”

Another long-time assistant, Miki D’Agostino, remains in Cincinnati with Pochettino for the Haiti match.

Advancement from the quarterfinals would cement the U.S.’s place in the March semifinals at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles while also clinching a place at the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup next summer.
